status: Evidence for a later waveform control, not a validated design or a queued fluid result

source.read_sections: Description: retracting meniscus and surface-tension rebound; detailed comparison of Figs3/4; internal wetting discussion

source_summary: The disclosed Lorentz actuation initially retracts the meniscus into the chamber. After force removal, surface tension can reverse motion and eject a drop. The description proposes smaller/faster drops than direct outward forcing, and emphasizes internal wetting. No numerical transfer to our nozzle is established.
implication: After the active500us delayed-retract control, a single inward pulse followed by release is a distinct hypothesis to examine. Do not equate the patent description with successful solder jetting through conductive steel.
limits: Our neutral/mirror wall treatment lacks advancing/receding angles, pinning and oxide skins; rebound/reattachment could be sensitive to these omissions.
No published current, field, nozzle or repetition result is being adopted from this patent.
The proposed test would need a matched zero-current control and enough recovery time; it is not just an electrical polarity check.

nearflush_175A_electrical_sensitivity.status: Budget only; no175A fluid case launched

driver.method: Exact integrals of piecewise-linear prescribed current; V=IR+L dI/dt. Head modeled as constant cold resistance. Four-quadrant current regulation assumed.
limitations: No PWM ripple, switching/gate losses, current-loop dynamics, bus/lead ringing or protection design.
No capacitor ESR/ripple rating or switch SOA/temperature qualification.
Input R and L assumptions must be replaced with measured assembled values; motional voltage is omitted from this lumped check.
Electrical compliance is not a droplet or repetition-rate prediction.

limits: Initial cold-field extrapolation: fixed geometry, conductivity, current paths and material properties; no thermal PDE or temperature-dependent resistance.
No phase change, external contact heating, rod/lead losses or cooling. Local maxima depend on the voxel resolution.
Diffusion length is sqrt(k*t/(rho*cp)), an order-of-magnitude scale, not a simulated temperature correction.
Repetition power assumes identical electrical pulses, not demonstrated repeatable droplet formation.
